observation_format.note: Tool results are plain strings in the shipped AgentExecutor example.

tool_call_format.note: Tools declared via LangChain4j/Spring AI @Tool annotations, dispatched through provider tool-calling.

tool_count.note: Tool set is user-supplied (toolsFromObject); no fixed default count.

edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool ships; tools are user-defined.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote:
@Tool(description = "tool for test AI agent executor")
String execTest( @ToolParam(description ="test message") String message )
tool_schema_source.note: Schemas derived from Java method signatures plus hand-written descriptions.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Spring Boot and Spring-native MCP / agent applications

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: We have implemented **AgentExecutor (aka ReACT Agent)** using LangGraph4j
loop_primitives.note: Graph engine also supports cyclical/conditional flows and streaming node events; react is the default AgentExecutor.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Explicit Control Flow:** Clearly define the paths and conditions for transitions between nodes in your graph.
planning_granularity.note: No plan object in AgentExecutor; control flow is graph-level, not an agent plan.

multi_agent_topology.note: Library supports multi-agent/subgraph composition: "building stateful, multi-agents applications"; default AgentExecutor is one agent.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Child Graphs (Subgraphs):** Compose complex graphs by nesting smaller, reusable graphs within nodes of a parent graph.
delegation_mechanism.note: Default AgentExecutor delegates to nobody; subgraph nesting is the reachable composition mechanism.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: invoke(S initialState, RunnableConfig config)`: Executes the graph and returns a `CompletableFuture<S>`
human_in_loop.note: No approval gate documented in the README; Studio allows manual inspection/run.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Manage and update a shared state across graph nodes, enabling memory and context awareness.
short_term_state.note: AgentState is a typed schema of channels/reducers beyond a message list.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: You'll typically use a `CheckpointSaver` implementation (e.g., `MemorySaver` for in-memory storage, or you can implement your own for persistent storage).
long_term_memory.note: Persistence is run/thread checkpointing, not cross-run memory re-injection.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Resuming:** Restore a graph to a previous state and continue execution.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Returns a `Map<String, Object>` representing updates to the state.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: an agent retrying a task or asking for clarification
retry_policy.note: Retries would be modelled as graph cycles by the user; model-level maxRetries(2) is transport-level.

rollback.note: State time-travel exists but no filesystem/git rollback of side effects.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: completes with the final state of the graph after it reaches an `END` node
termination_condition.note: Termination is graph reaching END, driven by the agent's decision not to call tools.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: The `RunnableConfig` can be used to pass in runtime configuration.
cost_controls.note: No cost or token budget documented.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Nodes and edges can be asynchronous (returning `CompletableFuture`), allowing for non-blocking I/O operations
timeouts.note: No timeout mechanism documented in the README.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: LangGraph4j is a Java library for building stateful, multi-agent applications with Large Language Models (LLMs).
execution_isolation.note: In-process Java library; tools are Java methods in the host JVM.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: return current number of system thread allocated by application
filesystem_access.note: Tools run in-process with host JVM privileges; no sandboxing documented.

permission_model.note: Registered tools are executed without authorisation checks.

tracing.evidence_quote: langgraph4j-opentelemetry/ # LangGraph4j Hook & OpenTelemetry integration module
tracing.note: Opt-in module; checkpoints and streamed state are available by default.

replayability.evidence_quote: Save the state of your graph at any point and replay or inspect it later.

eval_hooks.note: No benchmark evaluation runner in the repo structure listing; tests only.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Compilation validates the graph structure (e.g., checks for orphaned nodes).
guardrails.note: Validation is structural, not a safety guardrail.

target_domain.evidence_quote: designed to build sophisticated AI agentic architectures within the Java ecosystem

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Integrate with various LLM providers and custom Java logic.
model_agnostic.note: Via LangChain4j and Spring AI abstractions.
